thread:
Sam: quick question — we've got three different places applying 'model pin' semantics (hosted control plane, dedicated scheduler, and the private runtime). That duplication is causing rollbacks when we fallback between modes. Should we centralize pin intent in the control plane, or keep local runtime ownership?
Rachel: central sounds nice for hosted/dedicated (easier to reconcile, single audit trail). but private customers may be offline or air-gapped — can't rely on control plane there.
Dmitri: agree with Rachel. also worry about churn: if control plane is authoritative we need a resilient lease mechanism so a network blip doesn't evict pins. think signed leases + local TTLs.
Maya: another angle — what about a "declarative intent" model: control plane stores the intent (user asked to pin), runtimes hold enforcement leases derived from that intent. enforcement can be local for private.
Sam: that matches my thinking. sketch of proto API for intent:
```
POST /v1/pins
{
  "model": "redwood-13b-v2",
  "tenant": "acct-123",
  "intent": "pin",
  "priority": "served",
  "requested_by": "sam@redwood.com"
}
```
Rachel: +1. then runtimes can exchange a signed lease: control-plane signs a lease blob with expiry and baseline expected memory footprint. private runtimes validate signature locally and enforce.
Dmitri: edge cases: 1) control-plane unavailable and model needs to be unpinned (ops action) — local operator should be able to override with a customer-signed op. 2) model variants: when fallback happens, we need to surface the chain: intent->lease->enforcement variant. logs should include why a different variant was chosen.
Maya: runtime authn for private: use KMS-signed lease tokens (customer KMS) so control plane never sees plaintext in air-gapped install. For hosted/dedicated we use platform KMS.
Sam: good. for rollout strategy: proposed phased approach:
- phase 1: implement central intent store + signed lease API (hosted + dedicated). runtime uses leases, no enforcement change.
- phase 2: add local lease generation for Private with customer KMS integration and an "intent-sync tool" that can run offline.
- phase 3: add richer observability (per-lease audit, reason chain for fallback, token-level cost mapping).
Rachel: sounds practical. who wants to draft RFC?
Dmitri: I'll draft a short RFC covering lease format, fault modes, and transition plan.
Sam: great — tag me on the PR. can you include a tiny PoC sequence diagram for the offline flow?
Dmitri: yep. I'll include: intent post -> control-plane signs lease -> runtime validates; and offline: intent exported -> customer KMS signs local lease -> runtime enforces.
Maya: I'll prototype lease validation library in go-runtime and test variant-selection logging.
Sam: action items: Dmitri RFC, Maya POC, Rachel to scope telemetry needs. I'll open a ticket for API and link RFC.
Rachel: thanks. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rolling update: runtime/leases-service v1.2.0 -> v1.2.1 completed (no downtime)
Sam: nice, thanks bot :party_parrot:
